title: 📝 *GSC101 — GDB Solution 1*
text:
📝 *GSC101 — GDB Solution 1*

a) The statement is *Wrong.*

b) *Justification using Hund's Rule*

Mn²⁺ is used as an MRI contrast agent, but not because its electrons are paired. It is useful because all five of its d electrons are unpaired.

Manganese has atomic number 25.
Configuration: [Ar] 3d⁵ 4s²
Mn²⁺ (loses 2 electrons from 4s): [Ar] 3d⁵

According to Hund's rule, electrons first occupy separate orbitals with the same spin before pairing starts. Five d orbitals, five electrons → each orbital gets one electron. All five remain unpaired.

These unpaired electrons make Mn²⁺ *paramagnetic* — it responds to a magnetic field. This influences the relaxation of nearby water protons and improves contrast in MRI images.

So the statement is incorrect: Mn²⁺ has *five unpaired* electrons, not paired.
